_comment: Carry destination for issue #1067's remaining stages, W1067-G3 (the solver
half of the supply-temperature work) and W1067-G5b (the disinfection
switch's control half, split out of #1106 at fix review round 3). No roster
group in this tree claims #1067, so this file is those stages' brief. Shape
stage: W1067-G3, the solver half of #1067 (pricing the measured supply-temperature lift into the horizon behind its own flag); W1067-G5b, the disinfection switch's observe/control mode and switch control; W1067-G7, W1067-G7b-1 (the Modbus pre-fill module/options page and the device pre-fill resolver), and W1067-G7b-3 (the fuzzy fallback and the corpus measurement W1067-POST1's qualifying minimum is read from), for the closures-job carry below; W1067-POST1, the pre-fill offered during setup -- the config-flow half that shipped, and the constraints it puts on the runtime half the plan's POST1 section still owes

carries.from: W1067-G2, the learner half, whose own brief predicted that judging the efficiency reference against the measured lift would make the learned scale move less per sample
carries.control: The assumption invalidated: that a lift-aware efficiency REFERENCE slows cop_scale walking with the weather. It cannot. target_scale is cop_scale * commanded / measured, an expression the reference curve does not appear in, so no reference can move it. Measured on a 180-row grid (six outdoor temperatures x thirty consecutive folds) through the production _learn_measured_cop: a 55 degC supply reading against none separated zero rows of the cop_scale column. The null control ran the same grid at the merge base with no supply slot and diffed it byte for byte: identical.
carries.remeasure: Rebuild the grid at your own merge base: drive the production _learn_measured_cop through a shim carrying _flow_bias, once with observe_temps(55.0, 47.0) and once without, and diff the cop_scale column. Judge your own change on whether that column separates, because the learner half could not move it.
carries.brief: Pricing the lift is the only lever on cop_scale. The bias to apply is FlowCurveBias.bias_k in flow_lift.py, and the curve it was learned against is curve_supply_temp: call that function rather than re-deriving the curve, because a bias learned against one curve and spent against another is a silent offset. A bias with samples == 0 is exactly 0.0, and FlowCurveBias.from_dict enforces that on load, so it stays inert rather than being read as a measured zero. The bias is legitimate to spend only where the supply reading behind it was fresh and the interval space-dominant, which is what _fold_flow_lift gates on. The learner half ships no lift arithmetic: thermal_model.py is unchanged from main, and compute_cop's only lift is still the buffer term behind cop_flow_carnot. Fixtures: the learner half moved the five coordinator captures (six new heat_pump_signals keys each, all null or false) and config_flow, both claimed ADD-ONLY; every plan fixture is byte-identical. Yours will move solver fixtures, so claim that drift in tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt with its direction rather than re-recording it.

carries.from: W1067-G2 round 2 (#1068 review, comment 5703433010): the lift-aware reference double-counted the lift, and the owner chose to revert it (option 1)
carries.control: The model _learn_measured_cop holds is in its own comment: the heat the plan intended is commanded power times the modelled COP, and observed_cop = modelled_cop * commanded / measured. Under it the reference must be the COP the PLAN priced. A pump at supply S with true COP Ct = C0 * L(S) delivers the plan's heat at measured = commanded / L(S), and the ratio already carries the lift. Measured with the reviewer's lift_consistency.py (a pump generated from the model's own Carnot lift), at 8 degC outdoor and a 55 degC supply: the base credits 2.2285, the true COP, exactly. The lifted reference credited 1.3844, 37.9 % low (-24 to -38 % across -15..12 degC); the T4a residual read -2.2031 against -1.3590; and the envelope's thermal kW was 6.6856 against the true 10.7625. The null control at 35 degC, where L = 1, was identical in every column. tests/features.py pins the exact credit, 2.2285 mapped and unmapped.
carries.remeasure: Run lift_consistency.py (its source is in #1068's body and in comment 5703433010) at your merge base and your head, model 1, supplies 35 and 55, mapped and unmapped. Credited error must be 0 on every row at both ends, and the 35 degC rows identical. After pricing the lift, re-derive what the plan's COP is for a direct plant: if compute_cop then applies the curve-plus-bias lift, the reference follows that priced value automatically, because it is compute_cop(outdoor). Never feed it the measured supply.
carries.brief: Two constraints on the solver half. (1) The efficiency reference stays the COP the plan priced. When G3 prices the lift inside compute_cop, the reference inherits it. A second lift taken from the measured supply is the double count the review refuted. (2) The degradation watch (_observe_cop_health) is NOT lift-aware, and making it so is owed here, once the lift is priced. Measured on a healthy pump in one 3 degC bucket at 8 degC outdoor, supply 45 -> 55 degC: base and the shipped learner half show a +18.3 % false shortfall; feeding the watch observed_cop / L(S) while a fresh supply reading exists shows 0.0 %. But a normalised baseline fed ONE raw sample taken while the reading had lapsed shows +23.9 % (sample at 45 degC) or +37.9 % (at 55 degC): worse than doing nothing, and it drives the CUSUM on a compressor fault report. Two designs close that, each with a cost: (a) skip the watch when the supply slot is configured but has no fresh reading, which needs a configured-but-unreadable signal FlowCurveBias does not carry today, since last_supply_c is None for both unmapped and unreadable; (b) key normalised and raw samples into separate baselines, which changes the stored _cop_baseline key format and needs its migration. Either way there is a migration trap: every existing baseline is in RAW units, so the first normalised samples read as better than baseline until it re-anchors, which briefly masks a real decline. Whichever design ships must carry a measured stale-reading control: a lapsed reading must not produce a shortfall the healthy pump does not have.

carries.from: W1067-G3, the solver half (feat/1067-g3-flow-curve-cop): pricing the curve-plus-bias lift measured against the curve it prices from
carries.control: The model's weather curve sits below the 35 degC reference flow on the stock house, so the one-sided lift prices nothing there, and the bias clamp caps what it can price anywhere. Measured through ThermalModel.curve_flow_temp and ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor on the golden house (tests/golden.py house(), single zone, option on): curve 25.4 / 24.3 / 23.2 / 22.4 degC at -20 / -10 / 0 / 8 degC outdoor; lift factor at curve plus the full 15 K clamp 0.9266 / 0.9252 / 0.9247 / 0.9284, against 0.7809 / 0.7372 / 0.6777 / 0.6212 for a real 55 degC supply. With bias 0 and +5 K the priced COP equals the option-off COP exactly (tests/features.py pins it). Null control: on a house whose curve crosses the reference (3 kW pump, two 0.2 kW/K zones; 38.7 degC at -10 degC) the same option does price the lift, the plan's cost rises with the bias, and with the plant running at curve plus bias the learned cop_scale holds 1.0000 over 30 folds where the option off walks to 0.9417-0.9765.
carries.remeasure: Re-derive the curve temperatures and the clamp-edge lift factor at your own merge base with those two methods, on the golden house and on the owner's stored configuration, before claiming any gain. Drive the plant model of the #1068 reviewer's lift_consistency.py with the option on (the fixer's extension, lift_consistency_g3.py, is in the G3 pull request body): credited error must be 0 on every row, and the cop_scale column must hold at 1.0 only where the plant runs at the priced flow. Run it with the plant at 55 degC as the case that must stop walking.
carries.brief: What is legitimate next, and only under that control: either calibrate the weather curve itself against the measured supply, so that curve plus a small bias reaches the plant's real flow, or price the lift from the measured supply directly when a fresh reading exists. Refused without a new measurement: widening the 15 K bias clamp, whose bound is argued in flow_lift.py against probe errors, not against this ceiling. Either route must keep the efficiency reference equal to the COP the plan priced (the #1068 double count), keep compute_cop_dhw unlifted, keep batch parity with the scalar path, and keep the health watch's stale-reading control (a lapsed supply reading must add no shortfall a healthy pump does not have).

carries.from: W1067-G5a (pull request #1106), split from W1067-G5 at fix review round 3 (comment 5718114375, class missing-id-unload): the control half was cut from that pull request and is owed as W1067-G5b, so the write rule established there is a constraint on a stage that has not started
carries.control: The assumption narrowed: that a service call which returns without raising has landed its write. In BOOTED Home Assistant core 2026.2.3 it has not. The reviewer's round-3 instrument booted a real core (config entries, the real homeassistant integration with its blocking fan-out, real input_boolean entities and real template switches) and called the service the way the coordinator injects it, hass.services.async_call with blocking=True: against an entity id with NO STATE, core logs that the referenced entity is missing and RETURNS. Nothing is raised. An unload that treats that return as completion drops its ownership record, and the lifecycle probe on the real coordinator measured the consequence end to end - crash mid-boost with the switch on, restart before the switch's integration has loaded, reload inside the 30-minute grace - ending {"end": "on", "owned": [], "issues": [], "calls": ["turn_on", "turn_off"]}: left ON, no record, no repair. TWO null controls separate the real thing from its imitation. (a) A PRESENT entity whose write is rejected, same instrument, same call: owned_after holds the switch with failed set - so the missing-id result is about the missing state, not about the call. (b) The same lifecycle sequence WITHOUT the unload ends {"end": "off", "owned": [], "issues": []}. Why three review rounds passed over it: tests/hastub raises for an id with no state, and the round-2 stand-in raised for EVERY id, so both agreed with the wrong implementation. The stub's fidelity gap is recorded against fixer.md step 13 in #1106's body.
carries.remeasure: Every figure above is a snapshot of pull request #1106's head; re-establish the rule at your own merge base rather than quoting it. Boot a real Home Assistant core against the version your manifest pins, register a switch-domain entity and then remove its state, and call the same service the coordinator injects with blocking=True: assert on what the entity READS BACK, never on the absence of an exception. Run the present-but-rejected arm in the same pass as control (a) and require the two arms to separate; if they do not, your instrument is the round-2 stand-in again and proves nothing. Then drive the lifecycle sequence on the real coordinator with a fake whose missing-id branch RETURNS as core does, and require the no-unload arm as control (b). Check tests/ha_contract.py for the switch and service symbols you depend on before assuming tests/hastub models them, and extend the contract rather than shaping the stub to what your test needs.
carries.brief: The rule W1067-G5b must obey: a write counts as landed only when the target HAS A STATE BEFORE THE CALL and READS BACK the commanded state after it. A call that returned is not a write that landed. Refused without a new measurement: keying the ownership record, the unload path or any repair on the call's return value or on the absence of an exception - that is exactly the round-3 defect, and it is refused for the ON path as well as the unload path, because the same core behaviour produces a phantom ON record. The precondition on the safe alternative: an unload may drop its record only for an id that has a state at that moment; for an id with no state the record is KEPT, because the missing state means the switch's integration has not loaded, not that the switch is off. Also owed here, and unchanged by the split: any test standing in for core must RETURN for a missing id, since the stub raising is what made three rounds green. What G5a already shipped and G5b builds on: custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/disinfection.py reads the switch through the cycle's input reader and publishes {entity_id, state} only - it is observe-only, ships no mode option (a one-choice observe dropdown would be a control that does nothing), and never writes. Two observations the round-1 review of G5a recorded without blocking, both of which G5b inherits: an unreadable configured switch is named by the input watchdog's own attributes (input_health, problem_inputs), which is the house pattern for an optional slot and not a defect; and read_bool is lenient for flag domains, so a non-standard word on a switch entity reads as true - the shared reader's rule, which a control half must not assume away.

carries.from: W1067-G6 (pull request #1140), a required `closures` check red at both its heads
carries.control: The assumption narrowed: that a green `closures`/`closures-autofix` pair on a broad #1067-wave PR needs no local action beyond running the scoped gate. It does not hold when the PR's diff pulls BOTH tests/plan_view.py and one of tests/card.mjs / tests/card_drift.mjs into the same closure-scope batch: CI's `closures` job's full-arm re-record step (.github/workflows/tests.yml) iterates the scoped script list alphabetically and runs each script standalone, so tests/card.mjs and tests/card_drift.mjs -- which by design read the /tmp plandata file tests/plan_view.py writes earlier in a real tests/run.sh pass (tests/card.mjs's own header comment) -- record rc=1 (`FAIL: plan payload ... not found`) whenever both are batched together, regardless of any production change. Measured on PR #1140 (W1067-G6) at both `149ae6d` and its predecessor head: `closures-autofix` answers `skip-failed-recording` both times, refusing to merge ANY recording in the batch once one member failed, so a genuine, unrelated closure gap (there: tests/features.py newly importing heatpump_optimizer.sensor) cannot be auto-repaired even though the actual gap has nothing to do with card.mjs. Null control: origin/main's own tip (799d94e) shows `closures: success` at the same time -- that push's diff did not pull both script families into one batch, so the ordering gap is dormant on narrower diffs and does not fire universally.
carries.remeasure: After pushing, read `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`'s scope.run: if it names both tests/plan_view.py and either tests/card.mjs or tests/card_drift.mjs, expect the `closures` full-arm job to report rc=1 for the card lane(s) even with no card-code change, and `closures-autofix` to refuse with `skip-failed-recording` if there is ALSO a genuine closure gap elsewhere in the batch (there usually is, on a #1067-sized diff). Confirm by reading the `closures-autofix` job's own log rather than trusting the tick, per `ci-autofix.md`. If the batch has a real gap, do not wait for the bot: re-derive that ONE script's closure locally with `./tests/derive_closures.sh --single <script>` (Python lane only -- Darwin cannot record the node lanes via strace) and commit tests/closures.json yourself; verify with `python3 tests/closure.py record --out-dir <tmp> <script>` then `check --in-dir <tmp> --partial`.
carries.brief: Refused without a new measurement: editing tests/card.mjs or tests/card_drift.mjs to tolerate a missing plandata file, which would weaken a real check (it exists so the card markup under test is checked against THIS run's own plan, never a stale one from another checkout). Also refused: reordering or fixing .github/workflows/tests.yml's re-record loop from inside a feature PR -- that file is policy-adjacent (fixer.md opens it for the `policy` role's own budget) and any change to it needs the owner's approval before a merge, obtained via its own pull request, not bundled into #1067 work. What IS in scope for G7, G7b-1 (and G5b if its own diff is broad enough): recognise this exact shape (closures/closures-autofix both red, `skip-failed-recording` naming card.mjs or card_drift.mjs) as this known, unrelated ordering gap rather than a defect in the PR's own card work, and still track down and manually fix whatever OTHER genuine closure gap the batch surfaced -- the ordering gap never excuses a real one.

carries.from: W1067-G7b-3, the fuzzy fallback and its labelled corpus (branch feat/1067-g7b3-fuzzy-fallback): the measurement W1067-POST1's qualifying minimum is read from
carries.control: The assumption narrowed: that the corpus's per-device role counts can be read as one minimum over every device. They cannot. The fallback is defined to fill only the roles a source table left empty, and two of the corpus's eight devices are read by a table, so those two report zero fallback roles while being fully resolvable: the zeroes are the table's doing and not the device being unreadable. Measured on the corpus at custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/name_match.py's shipped pair, the fallback fills 0, 0, 4, 4, 2, 1, 5 and 4 roles across the eight devices in that order.
carries.remeasure: Run PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/measure_prefill_corpus.py at your own merge base and read its 'roles the fallback fills per corpus device' table. The minimum is the smallest count among the hand-shaped rows; a device with a source table is qualified by that table, not by this number, and the two generated rows print zero for exactly that reason.
carries.brief: W1067-POST1's qualification rule (docs/plan-1067-rotenso-inputs.md, 'Qualification'): a device qualifies only when a source G7b can map resolves it -- tuya_heat_pump, tuya_local with a supported model, or any integration where the fallback fills at least a minimum number of roles. That minimum is read from the hand-shaped rows of the table tools/measure_prefill_corpus.py prints over tests/fixtures/prefill_corpus.json, never from its zero rows, and the prompt's page is the pre-fill page W1067-G7b-1 built.

carries.from: W1067-POST1, the config-flow half (the pull request that carries this entry): the offer issue #1155 asks for is narrower than the offer the plan's own POST1 section designs, and only the narrower half ships
carries.control: The assumption narrowed: that "offer the pre-fill when a heat-pump device is added" means the runtime design docs/plan-1067-rotenso-inputs.md's W1067-POST1 section describes -- a per-device Store holding seen/offered/dismissed, a device-registry update listener registered in async_setup_entry, a repair issue raised through setpoint_check.create_issue, and withdrawal when a device is removed. Issue #1155 names the other surface beside the sentence -- the initial config flow -- and that is what shipped: one page, async_step_device_prefill in config_flow.py, reached from the second screen's submit when the switch is on and prefill_offer.offered() finds a device the G7b resolvers map, writing what the user keeps into the entry's own setup data rather than into options. Measured, and the instrument is its own null control: a driver dumping every step of the initial-flow walk with its rendered fields, placeholders, errors, menu, accumulated data and the entry it creates prints byte-identical output over a detached worktree of 2128a82 and over the branch head with the switch OFF, while the same walk with the switch ON lands on the device_prefill page instead of the finish_setup menu -- so the identity is not two empty dumps. Nothing of __init__.py, repairs.py or a Store was touched, and the switch is a stored option, CONF_PREFILL_OFFER in const.py, read only by config_flow.py.
carries.remeasure: Walk the initial flow at your own merge base with the registry holding a heat-pump device the G7b resolvers map, and require all three: with the switch off no pre-fill page renders and the wizard is the merge base's page for page; with the switch on the device_prefill page renders; and a device resolving nothing is offered nothing either way. The qualifying minimum is prefill_offer.QUALIFYING_MINIMUM, re-derived from tools/measure_prefill_corpus.py's roles-per-device table as the smallest count among its hand-shaped rows -- never read off the whole column and never quoted from here.
carries.brief: Anyone implementing the plan's wider POST1 design builds on this half, and four things bind. (1) There is ONE global switch. CONF_PREFILL_OFFER is it, read by _prefill_offer_stored as any entry's stored option; a runtime offer reads it the same way rather than adding a second key or a second page. (2) The qualification rule is prefill_offer's: qualifies() over device_prefill.resolve_with_fallback, a source table that resolved any role or the fallback filling QUALIFYING_MINIMUM of them. Do not re-derive it, and do not widen the matcher for it. (3) The offered page writes the wizard's data, not options: a runtime offer opens the same page but has an entry, so its write goes through the options save path (_save_or_menu and _omit_unstored_defaults) and must still write nothing unchanged. (4) The offer is off by default and read from the entries' options, so a first-time install is never offered the page -- the switch can only be turned on from an existing entry's pre-fill page. Changing that is an owner decision (the default, or asking the switch inside the flow), not a fixer's, and the plan's POST1 section still owes the per-device store, the listener, the repair issue and the withdrawal.
